module_title: Spice Blends from Around the World

lessons.title: Garam Masala: Regional Variations
lessons.body: Garam masala is a warming blend from India, but its exact recipe changes by region. In the north, it often includes black cardamom, cloves, and cinnamon. In the south, you might find more coriander, cumin, and curry leaves. For your African kitchen, start with a base: 4 tablespoons coriander seeds, 2 tablespoons cumin seeds, 1 tablespoon black peppercorns, 1 tablespoon cloves, 2 cinnamon sticks (about 3 inches each), and 1 tablespoon green cardamom pods. If you can get black cardamom, add 4 pods for a smoky note. Toast the whole spices in a dry pan over medium heat for 2-3 minutes until fragrant. Shake the pan constantly to avoid burning. Cool completely, then grind in a spice grinder or blender. Sift to remove coarse bits. Store in an airtight jar away from light for up to 3 months. Use 1-2 teaspoons per dish for rice, stews, or grilled meat. In West Africa, you can substitute grains of selim for cardamom and use local cinnamon. Adjust heat by adding dried chili. This blend is not a single recipe but a templateâtaste and tweak. For a smoky version, add 1 teaspoon smoked paprika. For a sweeter note, add 1 teaspoon fennel seeds. Always label with date. Making your own saves money and lets you control quality. Start with small batches to find your preferred balance.

lessons.title: Ras el Hanout: Moroccan Blend
lessons.body: Ras el Hanout means 'head of the shop' in Arabic, and it's a signature Moroccan blend that can include 20 or more spices. A practical home version uses: 2 tablespoons cumin, 2 tablespoons coriander, 1 tablespoon cinnamon, 1 tablespoon paprika, 1 tablespoon ginger, 1 tablespoon turmeric, 1 teaspoon black pepper, 1 teaspoon white pepper, 1 teaspoon allspice, 1 teaspoon nutmeg, 1 teaspoon cloves, 1 teaspoon cardamom, 1 teaspoon mace, and 1 teaspoon dried rose petals (optional). For a more authentic touch, add 1 teaspoon grains of paradise or 1 teaspoon cubeb pepper. Toast whole spices if you have them: cumin, coriander, and cardamom. Grind all ingredients together. Store in a dark jar. Use 1-2 teaspoons per kilogram of meat or vegetables. In tagines, add at the start with onions. In Africa, you can find many of these spices in local markets. If rose petals are unavailable, omit or use a pinch of lavender. This blend is warm, aromatic, and slightly sweet. It works well with lamb, chicken, and root vegetables. Make a small batch first to adjust ratios. For a spicier version, add 1 teaspoon cayenne. For a milder version, reduce black pepper. Always grind fresh for best flavor. Label and date. Use within 6 months.

lessons.title: Chinese Five-Spice: Balance of Flavors
lessons.body: Chinese five-spice powder balances sweet, sour, bitter, salty, and umami. The classic five ingredients are star anise, cloves, cinnamon, Sichuan peppercorns, and fennel seeds. A standard ratio: 2 tablespoons star anise, 1 tablespoon cloves, 1 tablespoon cinnamon (cassia), 1 tablespoon Sichuan peppercorns, and 1 tablespoon fennel seeds. Toast whole spices in a dry pan for 1-2 minutes until fragrant. Cool and grind. If you can't find Sichuan peppercorns, use black peppercorns plus a pinch of ground ginger. In Africa, star anise is available in many markets; if not, use anise seeds. This blend is strongâuse sparingly. For a 1 kg pork or beef roast, use 1 teaspoon. For stir-fries, use 1/4 teaspoon per serving. It also works in marinades for grilled fish or chicken. For a sweeter version, add 1 teaspoon brown sugar. For heat, add 1/2 teaspoon chili flakes. Store in an airtight container for up to 6 months. Make small batches because the flavor fades. Label with date. Experiment with local ingredients: cloves from Zanzibar are excellent. This blend is not just for Chinese foodâtry it in African stews for a new twist.

lessons.title: Herbes de Provence: French Blend
lessons.body: Herbes de Provence is a dried herb blend from southern France. Traditional ingredients: 2 tablespoons dried thyme, 2 tablespoons dried oregano, 2 tablespoons dried savory, 1 tablespoon dried rosemary, 1 tablespoon dried marjoram, 1 tablespoon dried basil, 1 teaspoon dried sage, and 1 teaspoon fennel seeds. Some versions include lavender flowersâuse 1 teaspoon if you like. In Africa, you can grow or buy these herbs locally. If savory is unavailable, use extra thyme. Mix all herbs in a bowl. Crush rosemary and fennel seeds slightly with a mortar and pestle to release flavor. Store in a glass jar away from light. Use 1-2 teaspoons per kilogram of chicken, fish, or vegetables. It's great in grilled meats, roasted potatoes, and tomato sauces. For a stronger flavor, rub the herbs between your palms before adding. This blend is mild, so you can use more than other spice mixes. For an African twist, add 1 teaspoon dried chili or 1 teaspoon ground ginger. Make a large batch and share with friends. Label and date. Use within 1 year for best flavor. This blend is perfect for beginners because it's forgivingâadjust amounts to taste.

lessons.title: Baharat: Middle Eastern Spice Mix
lessons.body: Baharat is a warm, aromatic spice blend used across the Middle East. A common version: 2 tablespoons black pepper, 2 tablespoons paprika, 1 tablespoon cumin, 1 tablespoon coriander, 1 tablespoon cloves, 1 tablespoon cinnamon, 1 tablespoon nutmeg, 1 tablespoon cardamom, and 1 teaspoon allspice. Some recipes add 1 tablespoon dried mint or 1 tablespoon ginger. Toast whole spices (cumin, coriander, cardamom, cloves) in a dry pan for 2 minutes. Cool and grind with the rest. In Africa, you can find these spices in bulk. Use 1-2 teaspoons per kilogram of lamb, beef, or chicken. It's excellent in kebabs, rice pilafs, and stews. For a spicier version, add 1 teaspoon cayenne. For a sweeter version, add 1 teaspoon sugar. Store in an airtight jar for up to 6 months. Make small batches because the flavor fades. Label with date. This blend is versatileâtry it on roasted vegetables or grilled fish. It also works as a dry rub. Adjust the black pepper to your taste. In North Africa, baharat is similar to ras el hanout but simpler. Experiment with local spices like grains of selim for a unique twist.

lessons.title: Za'atar: Middle Eastern Herb and Spice Blend
lessons.body: Za'atar is a Middle Eastern blend of dried herbs, sesame seeds, and sumac. The classic ratio: 1/4 cup dried thyme, 2 tablespoons toasted sesame seeds, 2 tablespoons sumac, and 1 teaspoon salt. Some versions use oregano or marjoram instead of thyme. In Africa, you can grow thyme or use local dried herbs. Sumac is tangy and red; if unavailable, substitute 1 tablespoon lemon zest mixed with 1 teaspoon salt. Toast sesame seeds in a dry pan until golden, about 2 minutes. Cool. Mix all ingredients. Store in an airtight jar for up to 6 months. Use za'atar as a dip with olive oil and bread, or sprinkle on hummus, salads, and grilled meats. For a spicy version, add 1/2 teaspoon chili flakes. For a lemony boost, add 1 teaspoon dried lemon peel. This blend is easy to make and very forgiving. Start with the base recipe and adjust. In North Africa, za'atar is less common but gaining popularity. Make a batch and share. Label with date. Use within 3 months for best flavor. It's a great way to add flavor without heat.

quiz.q: What is the primary difference between northern and southern Indian garam masala?
options: A) Northern uses more coriander, southern uses more cumin
B) Northern often includes black cardamom and cloves, southern uses more coriander and curry leaves
C) Northern is always spicy, southern is always sweet
D) Northern uses no cinnamon, southern uses cinnamon
quiz.explanation: Regional variations in garam masala reflect local ingredients and tastes, with northern versions often featuring black cardamom and southern versions using more coriander and curry leaves.

quiz.q: How many spices can traditional ras el hanout include?
quiz.explanation: Ras el hanout is known for its complex blend, often containing 20 or more spices.

quiz.q: What are the five flavors balanced in Chinese five-spice?
options: A) Sweet, sour, bitter, salty, umami
B) Hot, cold, warm, cool, neutral
C) Sweet, spicy, tangy, smoky, earthy
D) Salty, sweet, sour, bitter, pungent
quiz.explanation: Chinese five-spice aims to balance the five basic tastes: sweet, sour, bitter, salty, and umami.

quiz.q: Which herb is NOT typically in Herbes de Provence?
quiz.explanation: Herbes de Provence typically includes thyme, rosemary, oregano, savory, marjoram, and basil, but not mint.

quiz.q: What is a common ingredient in baharat?
quiz.explanation: Black pepper is a key ingredient in baharat, along with paprika, cumin, coriander, and others.

quiz.q: What gives za'atar its tangy flavor?
quiz.explanation: Sumac is the traditional ingredient that provides za'atar's characteristic tangy taste.

quiz.q: How should you store garam masala?
options: B) In an airtight jar away from light
C) In a plastic bag in the sun
quiz.explanation: Airtight jars away from light preserve the flavor of garam masala for up to 3 months.

quiz.q: What is a good substitute for sumac in za'atar?
quiz.explanation: Lemon zest mixed with salt can mimic sumac's tangy and salty profile.

quiz.q: How much Chinese five-spice should you use for 1 kg of meat?
quiz.explanation: Chinese five-spice is potent, so 1 teaspoon per kilogram of meat is sufficient.

quiz.q: Which spice is NOT typically in baharat?
quiz.explanation: Fennel is not a common ingredient in baharat; it is more typical in Chinese five-spice or Herbes de Provence.

quiz.q: What is the main herb in traditional za'atar?
quiz.explanation: Thyme is the primary herb in traditional za'atar, though oregano or marjoram can be used.

quiz.q: How long should you toast whole spices for garam masala?
quiz.explanation: Toasting for 2-3 minutes over medium heat until fragrant is ideal to avoid burning.

quiz.q: Which spice is a key difference in northern vs. southern garam masala?
quiz.explanation: Black cardamom is more common in northern garam masala, giving a smoky note.

quiz.q: What does 'ras el hanout' mean?
quiz.explanation: Ras el hanout translates to 'head of the shop', indicating the best spices a merchant offers.

quiz.q: Which ingredient is optional in ras el hanout?
quiz.explanation: Rose petals are optional and add a floral note to ras el hanout.

quiz.q: What is a good substitute for Sichuan peppercorns in Chinese five-spice?
quiz.explanation: Black peppercorns plus a pinch of ground ginger can replace Sichuan peppercorns.

quiz.q: How much Herbes de Provence should you use per kilogram of chicken?
quiz.explanation: Herbes de Provence is mild, so 1-2 teaspoons per kilogram is a good starting point.

quiz.q: Which herb is NOT part of traditional Herbes de Provence?
quiz.explanation: Dill is not typically included in Herbes de Provence; savory and marjoram are.

quiz.q: What is a common addition to baharat for heat?
quiz.explanation: Cayenne can be added to baharat to make it spicier.

quiz.q: How should you store za'atar?
options: B) In an airtight jar for up to 6 months
quiz.explanation: Za'atar keeps well in an airtight jar away from light for up to 6 months.

quiz.q: What is the typical ratio of thyme to sumac in za'atar?
options: B) 2 parts thyme to 1 part sumac
C) 1 part thyme to 2 parts sumac
D) 4 parts thyme to 1 part sumac
quiz.explanation: A classic ratio is 1/4 cup thyme to 2 tablespoons sumac, which is 2:1.

quiz.q: Which spice blend is known for balancing five flavors?
quiz.explanation: Chinese five-spice is specifically designed to balance sweet, sour, bitter, salty, and umami.

quiz.q: What is a common use for baharat?
options: A) In kebabs and rice pilafs
quiz.explanation: Baharat is commonly used in savory dishes like kebabs and rice pilafs.

quiz.q: How long can you store homemade garam masala?
quiz.explanation: For best flavor, use garam masala within 3 months.

quiz.q: Which ingredient is used in both Chinese five-spice and garam masala?
quiz.explanation: Cloves are common to both Chinese five-spice and garam masala.

quiz.q: What is a good African substitute for cardamom in garam masala?
quiz.explanation: Grains of selim (also known as Ethiopian cardamom) can substitute for cardamom.

quiz.q: How much za'atar should you use for a dip?
options: A) 1 tablespoon per cup of olive oil
quiz.explanation: A common ratio for za'atar dip is 1 tablespoon of za'atar mixed with 1/4 cup olive oil.

quiz.q: Which spice blend includes dried rose petals?
quiz.explanation: Rose petals are an optional ingredient in ras el hanout.

quiz.q: What is the main difference between baharat and ras el hanout?
options: A) Baharat is simpler and less complex
C) Ras el hanout has no cinnamon
D) Baharat is only for lamb
quiz.explanation: Baharat is generally a simpler blend compared to the complex ras el hanout.

quiz.q: How should you adjust Chinese five-spice for a sweeter version?
quiz.explanation: Adding a little brown sugar can make Chinese five-spice sweeter.
